subject: northern quoll
title: Every Male of This Animal Dies Before Its Second Birthday

scenes.text: In this species, almost no male lives to see a second year.
The northern quoll is a spotted Australian hunter the size of a kitten.
Males mature at eleven months. Then the mating season starts, and they stop resting.
One tracked male walked over six miles in a single night searching for females.
They lose weight and fur, and most die within two weeks of mating.
Females live up to three years. Every male gets exactly one season.

description:
Male northern quolls mature at about 11 months, mate once, and almost all die within weeks, around one year old.
Researchers tracked one male walking 10.4 km in a night; a 2023 study linked the die-off to lack of sleep and exhaustion. Females can live up to three years.
Would you trade your whole life for one season?
first_comment: Scientists are also training young quolls not to eat poisonous cane toads, and trained ones survived up to five times longer. Have you ever seen a quoll?
